title: Search filter numeric attributes: SearchUtils._get_value returns int or float; only experiment and evaluation-dataset builders reject fractional values
answers: Why do run start_time filters fail with psycopg v3 on PostgreSQL when the value is a plain number?
Why does a fractional creation_time filter on experiments raise an error while the same filter on runs is accepted?
Where is the numeric value of an attribute filter like start_time or created_at parsed?
How are fractional logged-model creation_timestamp comparisons evaluated in memory?
Does the MCP registry created_at filter accept fractional values?
body:
Path: Parses the right-hand side of attribute comparisons in search filter strings (run attributes.start_time, experiment creation_time, evaluation-dataset created_time, logged-model creation_timestamp, MCP registry created_at) through mlflow/utils/search_utils.py:SearchUtils._get_value; the parsed condition dicts feed the SQL filter builders and the in-memory matchers.
Rule: _get_value returns int for integer literal tokens and float for other numeric tokens, instead of the raw string. The in-memory matchers (SearchUtils._does_run_match_clause, SearchUtils._does_logged_model_match_clause, SearchUtils._does_model_match_clause) call int() only when the value is still a str, so fractional comparisons stay exact (1.5 neither equals nor truncates to 1). The integer-only check is not in the shared parser: mlflow/store/tracking/sqlalchemy_store.py:_get_search_experiments_filter_clauses and _get_search_datasets_filter_clauses raise invalid_parameter_value when the value is a float.
Symptom: On PostgreSQL with the psycopg v3 driver, run start_time and MCP registry timestamp filters bound a string against an integer column and errored, because the parser left numeric tokens as strings.
Constraints: Applies only to numeric attribute keys; string and identifier values are unchanged. Do not add a float rejection to the run, logged-model or MCP builders, since they compare fractions exactly on purpose. Experiment and dataset searches keep their integer-only validation.
applies: Search filter parsing and SQL/in-memory matching for numeric attributes across tracking stores (runs, experiments, datasets, logged models, MCP registry).
says: Searching runs by start time fails on PostgreSQL databases due to type mismatch errors.
Numeric timestamp search filters should be treated as numbers rather than text strings.
Filtering experiments by fractional creation times should produce a clear validation error.
Run search filters with decimal values truncate or fail instead of matching exact numbers.
Allow searching logged models and runs using decimal numbers without losing precision.
search: In search filter parsing across tracking stores, SearchUtils._get_value in mlflow/utils/search_utils.py returns int for integer tokens and float for other numeric tokens instead of raw strings. In-memory matchers (SearchUtils._does_run_match_clause, SearchUtils._does_logged_model_match_clause, SearchUtils._does_model_match_clause) only cast to int when the value is a string, preserving exact fractional comparisons for runs, logged models, and MCP registry timestamps. Integer-only validation is enforced specifically in mlflow/store/tracking/sqlalchemy_store.py via _get_search_experiments_filter_clauses and _get_search_datasets_filter_clauses, which raise invalid_parameter_value on float inputs. This guidance applies only to numeric attribute keys, leaving string and identifier tokens unchanged and forbidding float rejections in run, logged-model, or MCP builders.
